Upgrade Flow

Plan a firmware maintenance window for many appliances as one staged workflow — bulk pre-upgrade evidence, one change request, a scheduled rollout in rounds, and live execution progress.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsbackups.create backups.restore users.manage
📍 WhereAutomation → Upgrade Flow (FortiWeb ADOM) (URL /web/upgrade-flow/)

What is it?#

The Upgrade Flow treats a firmware maintenance window as one workflow instead of a per-appliance chore. On one page you pre-flight every appliance in the window, raise one change request that cites all of that evidence, plan how many appliances go down at a time, and then watch execution appliance by appliance.

The page owns no workflow of its own: the pre-flight is the same one the per-appliance Upgrade Preparation page runs, and the change request is created through the same path as Change Requests.

What does it do?#

The page is organised in numbered stages:

  1. 1Pre-upgrade (bulk)Choose the destination version, tick appliances, run a read-only pre-flight on each; one stored run per appliance
  2. 2Change request (CRQ)Raise ONE change of type upgrade citing the runs you choose — or split the selection into waves
  3. 3The change itselfThe raised change is shown in full on the same page: approve, schedule, notify, export, read the document
  4. 4Scheduled rolloutDecide how many appliances per round and the gap; saved as real scheduled tasks once approved
  5. 5ExecutionPer-appliance progress page, polled live, with a Start now button inside the window
  • Stage 1 — Pre-upgrade (bulk) — described in this article.
  • Stages 2 and 3 — see Upgrade Flow: change request and waves.
  • Stage 4 and execution — see Upgrade Flow: rollout and execution.

❗Important — The upgrade executor does not flash firmware in this release

When a scheduled upgrade fires, every appliance is reported with "Firmware upgrade for <appliance> is not executed by the headless service layer (no upgrade runbook); no firmware was flashed." and is graded failed. The Upgrade Flow is therefore a planning, evidence and change-control tool; the actual flash is done per appliance from the Firmware page. See rollout and execution.

Requirements#

  • At least one registered FortiWeb appliance. The flow covers only the products that the Upgrade preparation (backup + health) scheduled action pre-flights and that the change's upgrade action can flash — today FortiWeb. The page says so: This flow covers fortiweb: the products whose firmware SATOM can flash from a change. FortiADC has no flash path, so its pre-upgrade runs from the appliance page only. For a FortiADC, run Upgrade Prep on the appliance page (see Firmware upgrade).
  • The destination version must be known to the console: an uploaded upgrade image, a version already running in the fleet, or a version declared by hand under Firmware → API versions (see Firmware). An uploaded image is not required to pre-flight.
  • For the configuration backup step: a working backup path to the appliance (see Backups). For the health battery on FortiWeb: SSH access.

Permissions#

Action Required permission
Open the page, run the pre-upgrade sweep, open the execution progress page backups.create or backups.restore (the legacy backup permission)
Stage 2 (raise the change, raise waves), stage 3, stage 4 (save rollout), Start now users.manage
  • Users with only the backup permissions see stage 1 and the Batched rollouts list; the stage 2–4 cards are not rendered at all. Pressing Start now or posting a change without users.manage returns 403.
  • The sidebar entry is shown only in the FortiWeb ADOM, and only when you hold the backup permission and the Automation group is visible to you (the group itself needs any configuration-write permission, e.g. appliances.edit). With the default profiles: Operator can use stage 1; Administrator can use every stage; Viewer cannot open the page (403).
  • The appliance list shows only appliances visible to you: the active ADOM's products, and no maintenance-mode appliances unless you hold appliances.view_maintenance.

See also Permissions.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the flow covers FortiWeb only (FortiADC used to be offered at stage 1 and then refused at stage 2), and stage 1 lists each multi-ADOM FortiWeb once, on the row that owns the device.

How to use#

Open the flow#

  1. In the FortiWeb ADOM, open Automation → Upgrade Flow.
  2. Or, from an appliance's Upgrade Preparation page, answer "Is this appliance part of a full upgrade window?" with Full upgrade flow — the flow opens with that appliance ticked. The Raise change request button next to a recorded run opens the flow with the appliance ticked and that run pre-chosen as its evidence.

A blue banner confirms a hand-off: "Pre-selected from its pre-upgrade page: <appliance>". If the link names an appliance or run that is not on the list, an amber banner says so instead of silently ticking nothing.

Run the pre-upgrade sweep (stage 1)#

  1. In Upgrade to, choose the destination version. This is required. Each option shows image uploaded or no image uploaded, already in the fleet when an appliance runs it, moves N/M (how many comparable appliances it would upgrade), and which appliances are already there or ahead. Versions declared only as a line (for example 8.0) are grouped under Line only — no patch level declared.
  2. Choose what to measure (all ticked by default): - Config backup — a configuration backup into the backup vault. - Health battery (SSH) — a system health read. - Service validation — an HTTP baseline probe of every published service.
  3. Tick the appliances in the window (the header checkbox ticks all). When the chosen version cannot move a ticked appliance forward, the reason appears in red under its name before you submit.
  4. Click Run pre-upgrade on selected.

The sweep runs one appliance at a time and covers at most 40 appliances. Long sweeps continue as a background job (see Result).

Read the appliance table#

Column Meaning
Appliance Name (links to the appliance) and management host; a red hint if the chosen version would skip it
Product Appliance product
Latest pre-upgrade Newest stored run (#id and UTC time, links to the Upgrade Preparation page), or never run
Move current → destination as recorded on the newest run, with the Upgrade Advisory's verdict for that move; no destination recorded for a run that stored none
Evidence this change cites Which stored run (up to the 10 newest) the change in stage 2 will cite for this appliance, each marked passed or not clean; or no run cited for this appliance

The Upgrade Advisory badge (shown as Scout until 2026-10-14) reads blocker, caution, clear, unknown (the Upgrade Advisory read the release notes and found nothing on this move) or unavailable (it could not read them). It may add counts (blocking · caution) and hop(s) with no harvested notes. The verdict is computed each time the page is drawn, so newly harvested release notes change it without re-running the sweep. The Upgrade Advisory is available while Path Diagnostics is switched on (Settings → Path Diagnostics). See Release notes.

Beside the move, each appliance also shows its migration verdict — ready, ready with warnings, blocked or cannot assess — for that move: whether its configuration (from its newest configuration backup) survives the destination build. The badge links to the full Migration report. The comparison of two builds is computed once per move; at most 20 appliances are assessed per page render, the others link to their report.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Upgrade to Destination version, stored on every run of this sweep Yes 8.0.5
Config backup Take a configuration backup No (default on) ticked
Health battery (SSH) Read a health baseline No (default on) ticked
Service validation Probe every published service as a baseline No (default on) ticked
Appliance checkboxes Appliances to pre-flight (max 40 per sweep) Yes, at least one fweb-01, fweb-02
Evidence this change cites Run cited per appliance in stage 2 No #42 · 2026-10-01 21:04 UTC · passed

Example#

🧪Example — Three FortiWeb appliances, one already upgraded

fweb-01 and fweb-02 run 7.6.8; fweb-03 already runs 8.0.5.

  1. Upgrade to offers 8.0.5 · image uploaded · already in the fleet · moves 2/3 · fweb-03 already there or ahead.
  2. You tick all three and run the sweep.
  3. fweb-03 is skipped: "fweb-03 cannot be upgraded to 8.0.5: it is already running it, so there is no upgrade to pre-flight. It was skipped; the rest of the sweep ran."
  4. The summary reads "Pre-upgrade swept 2 appliance(s) towards 8.0.5: 2 clean, 0 ran but not clean, 0 could not be pre-flighted. 1 skipped: already on 8.0.5 or past it."
  5. Continue with stage 2 for fweb-01 and fweb-02.

Result#

  • One stored pre-upgrade run per swept appliance, recording the firmware it was running, the destination, a pass/not-clean verdict and summary, the full result (backup, health, maintenance permission, service probes) and the inventory of published services the window affects. Runs appear in the appliance table and on each appliance's Upgrade Preparation page.
  • The verdict is not clean when a requested backup or health check failed, the service sweep could not run at all, or the account lacks the maintenance permission. Individual unreachable services do not fail the run — they are recorded as the baseline. When a destination is set, the summary also reports an offline API-surface comparison against that version (reported, never graded).
  • A configuration backup appears in the backup vault for each appliance where Config backup was ticked.
  • The page reloads with the destination re-selected and a summary flash (green when everything was clean, amber otherwise), followed by one red flash per appliance that could not be pre-flighted and one amber flash per appliance that ran but was not clean.
  • An audit entry upgrade_flow.prep_sweep records the destination and the clean / not-clean / failed / skipped counts (Audit log).
  • If the sweep takes longer than a couple of seconds it continues as a background job; the browser waits on the job and then shows the same result. See Jobs.

Troubleshooting#

"Choose the version this window upgrades TO before running the sweep."#

Possible causes - Upgrade to was left on — choose the destination version —.

Solution 1. Pick a destination version and run the sweep again. Nothing was started.

Verification - The summary flash names the version: "Pre-upgrade swept N appliance(s) towards <version>…".

"… is not a version this console knows of, so nothing here can review the move to it."#

Possible causes - The version is not in the firmware catalogue (no image, not running anywhere, not declared).

Solution 1. Declare it under Firmware → API versions, or upload its image (see Firmware). 2. Reload the Upgrade Flow; the version appears in Upgrade to.

Verification - The version is listed in the Upgrade to select.

"This console knows of no firmware version for these products yet, so no sweep can be run."#

Possible causes - No image, running version or declared version exists for FortiWeb.

Solution 1. Upload an image or declare the version under Firmware → API versions.

Verification - The Upgrade to select lists at least one version.

"This console knows of N firmware version(s) for these products, and none of them is newer than what any appliance below is running"#

Possible causes - Every known version is equal to or older than what the listed appliances run.

Solution 1. Declare or upload a later release under Firmware → API versions.

Verification - A version with moves N/M appears in the select.

"… would not move any of these appliances forward"#

Possible causes - The posted version is at or below every comparable appliance on the page.

Solution 1. Pick a later version, or sweep the appliances that are still behind.

Verification - The sweep summary flash appears instead of the refusal.

"Nothing was started: not one of the N selected appliance(s) would move forward to …"#

Possible causes - Every ticked appliance already runs the destination version or something newer. Each one is listed in its own red flash.

Solution 1. Pick a later version, or tick an appliance that is still behind it.

Verification - The red hints under the appliance names disappear for the ticked rows.

"… cannot be upgraded to …: it is already running …, which is newer — that move is a DOWNGRADE"#

Possible causes - The version chosen for the whole window is older than what this appliance runs. The appliance was skipped; the rest of the sweep ran.

Solution 1. If the appliance belongs in this window, choose a later destination. Otherwise untick it. Downgrades are not reviewed by this pre-flight.

Verification - The next sweep has no skipped count for that appliance.

"N appliances selected; one sweep covers at most 40. Run it in batches — nothing was started."#

Possible causes - More than 40 appliances were ticked.

Solution 1. Tick at most 40 appliances, run the sweep, then run the rest in another sweep towards the same version.

Verification - The summary flash reports the sweep.

"The pre-upgrade does not run against …"#

Possible causes - A ticked appliance is of a product the pre-upgrade does not support.

Solution 1. Untick it. Supported products are listed in the message (FortiWeb). For a FortiADC, run Upgrade Prep from the appliance page instead.

Verification - The sweep starts.

"One or more selected appliances do not exist or are not visible to you. Nothing was started."#

Possible causes - An appliance was deleted, moved into maintenance mode, or belongs to another ADOM since the page was loaded.

Solution 1. Reload the page and tick the appliances again.

Verification - The sweep summary appears.

"No appliance of a type the pre-upgrade supports is visible to you."#

Possible causes - No FortiWeb appliance is registered in the active ADOM, or all are in maintenance mode.

Solution 1. Register an appliance (see Appliances) or switch to the right ADOM.

Verification - The appliance table lists your appliances.

"Pre-upgrade acts on the whole appliance; run it on the device row, not on ADOM row(s) …"#

Possible causes - A posted selection named an ADOM row of a multi-ADOM FortiWeb. The pre-upgrade backs up and flashes the whole box, so it runs on the row that owns the device.

Solution 1. Reload the page and tick the device row (the only row of that appliance the list shows).

Verification - The sweep summary appears.

An appliance shows "<name>: the run completed but could not be stored" or an error#

Possible causes - The pre-flight ran but the run could not be saved, or the appliance raised an error (unreachable, authentication). The sweep continued with the other appliances.

Solution 1. Fix connectivity (see Device health) and run the sweep again for that appliance only, towards the same version.

Verification - The appliance's Latest pre-upgrade shows a new run.

Advanced#

Advanced How the destination list is built
  • Versions come from the firmware catalogue for each supported product, sorted newest first. Only upgrade images count as "image uploaded"; install images (.zip, .qcow2, .ova) do not.
  • A version is hidden only when the page can prove it is not an upgrade for any listed appliance of the same product. Versions are compared per product and numerically per component (8.0.10 is newer than 8.0.9). A line-only version, an appliance whose firmware was never read, or a page with no comparable appliance keeps the version on the list.
  • When every appliance's newest run declares the same destination, that version is pre-selected on your next visit.
Advanced What is skipped and what is swept

Per ticked appliance, the sweep skips it only when it provably already runs the destination (same) or something newer (behind, a downgrade). Appliances of another product, with unreadable firmware, or where the comparison is undecided are swept. Nothing is stored for a skipped appliance.

Advanced Limits
Limit Value
Appliances per sweep 40 (refused, never truncated)
Runs offered per appliance in the evidence chooser 10 newest
Sweep order Sequential, by appliance name
Advanced One row per chassis

A FortiWeb in ADOM mode is registered once per ADOM. Like the per-appliance Upgrade Preparation page, the Upgrade Flow lists and sweeps only the row that owns the device-wide actions (the root row, or the first by name; see Appliances). The other ADOM rows are the same box and are not listed.
